answer: One defense is a refundable stake tied to each agent identity. A new agent locks a deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed if peers catch it lying about a delivery or double-selling a service. A willow branch bends in wind without snapping, but a fake identity still has to pay the same deposit as a real one, so spinning up a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand deposits. A single plume of fake reviews cannot outweigh a long record of completed trades, and each caught fraud sends a ripple through the agent rating that other agents can check before they deal with it.
